<system-reminder>
## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

title: 'Fixed #32091 -- Fixed admin search bar width on filtered admin page.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  On narrow screens, Django admin users who search within a filtered changelist can end up with a search box that collapses to an unusably small width. That makes refining results frustrating exactly when filters are already in use.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keep the admin search input at a practical width on filtered changelist pages, even in the responsive layout.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When a changelist is opened with a search query on the filtered page, the `searchbar` element keeps a visible usable width rather than shrinking to a tiny control; the regression test specifically guards that it stays wider than 50 pixels.

  '

title: Avoided direct styles in admin templates.
category: other
requirement: 'Django admin pages should remain usable in deployments that enforce a strict Content Security Policy and reject inline styles. The hidden username inputs used on the admin password change and password reset confirmation screens still need to be present for browser password-manager behavior, but they should no longer depend on inline `style` attributes to stay out of sight. Those fields should instead render with the shared `hidden` CSS class, including markup such as `<input class="hidden" autocomplete="username" value="jsmith">`, so the pages keep the same behavior without violating CSP rules.

  '

title: 'Fixed #32034 -- Removed redundant get_app_config() call in AdminSite.app_index.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  An admin user opening an app index page expects the page title to come from the app information Django has already assembled for that page. This change is internal cleanup in a user-facing area: Django is doing an extra app-config lookup that is redundant and should not alter what admins see.


  ## Desired outcome

  Simplify admin app-index title generation so it reuses the app name already present in the page context, while keeping the visible page title and behavior unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `AdminSite.app_index` no longer performs the redundant app-config lookup, and the rendered title still follows the `''%(app)s administration''` pattern using the app name already stored in the app list context.

  '

  On narrow screens, Django admin users who search within a filtered changelist can end up with a search box that collapses to an unusably small width. That makes refining results frustrating exactly when filters are already in use.

title: 'Fixed #31880 -- Made QuerySet.aggregate() raise FieldError when aggregating over aggregation aliases.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Django developer building summary queries expects `QuerySet.aggregate()` to reject nonsensical expressions the same way annotated aggregates already do. At the moment it is possible to aggregate over an alias that is itself an aggregate, which produces confusing behavior instead of a clear validation error.


  ## Desired outcome

  If an aggregate in `QuerySet.aggregate()` references another aggregate alias from the same call, Django should stop early and explain that the referenced name is already an aggregate.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Attempting patterns like computing `Avg(''age'')` from an alias that was defined as an aggregate in the same `aggregate()` call raises `FieldError` with the contract message `Cannot compute Avg(''age''): ''age'' is an aggregate` instead of silently proceeding or failing obscurely later.

  '

title: 'Fixed #31636 -- Made BooleanFieldListFilter respect Field.choices.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Django admin user may filter a changelist by a nullable `BooleanField` that uses custom `choices`, expecting the sidebar labels to match the domain language used in the application instead of generic Yes/No text.


  ## Desired outcome

  `BooleanFieldListFilter` should respect `Field.choices` when building its options, including the labels for true, false, and null values. A field like `availability` should therefore present labels such as `Paid`, `Free`, and `Obscure` while still producing the standard query strings that the changelist expects.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The filter title should remain the field name, selections should use the usual parameters like `?availability__exact=0`, `?availability__exact=1`, and `?availability__isnull=True`, and the displayed option text should come from the field''s configured choices rather than Django''s default Yes/No/Unknown labels.

  '

  '

title: 'Fixed #32159 -- Ensured AsyncRequestFactory correctly sets headers.'
category: bugfix
requirement: 'Developers testing ASGI views with `AsyncRequestFactory` should be able to pass extra HTTP headers the same way they describe them in the request, without the synchronous client’s `HTTP_` prefix convention getting in the way. When code supplies values such as `AUTHORIZATION=''Bearer faketoken''` or `X_ANOTHER_HEADER=''some other value''`, those headers should appear on the resulting request with the expected lowercase HTTP names and corresponding `META` entries, so async tests exercise the same header flow a real ASGI request would. The goal is that `AsyncRequestFactory` correctly sets extra headers instead of silently dropping or mis-formatting them.

  '

  ticket-32223

title: 'Fixed #31907 -- Fixed missing validate_key() calls in cache backends.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Django developer expects cache key validation warnings to apply consistently across cache operations, not only to a small subset of methods.


  ## Desired outcome

  Backends that already validate keys should do so for all user-facing operations that accept keys, including `get()`, `touch()`, `delete()`, and `delete_many()`. Invalid keys should therefore trigger the same validation behavior no matter which cache method the application uses.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Calling these cache APIs with an invalid key should surface the standard validation warning or error instead of bypassing `validate_key()` for some methods while enforcing it for others.

  '

title: 'Fixed #29867 -- Added support for storing None value in caches.'
category: bugfix
requirement: 'Django cache users need `None` to be treated as a real cached value rather than as a signal that the key is missing. Cache operations such as `cache.get_many()`, `get_or_set()`, `has_key()`, `incr()`, `decr()`, `incr_version()`, and `decr_version()` should correctly distinguish between a stored `None` and an absent entry, so applications can cache null-like results without breaking follow-up logic. The only exception is the deprecated `MemcachedCache` backend, where the historical behavior must remain because the underlying `python-memcached` client cannot support this distinction.

  '

2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Django developers calling management commands programmatically rely on `call_command()` to satisfy required mutually exclusive options the same way the command line does. 7

14

16	
17	  '

7

11	
12

15	  A queryset that groups while annotating with a `Case()` expression containing no cases executes correctly, so the empty `Case()` no longer breaks grouping logic.
16	
17	  '

2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A Django project may still use `default_app_config` in an app package that has an empty `apps` module or no `apps` module at all while migrating toward the newer AppConfig discovery rules.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Populating the app registry should no longer crash in those layouts. 11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Projects with packages like `explicit_default_config_empty_apps` or `explicit_default_config_without_apps` should load cleanly under the deprecation path, emitting the expected `RemovedInDjango41Warning` message instead of crashing during app population.
16	
17	  '

1	title: 'Fixed #31826 -- Made AlterField operation a noop when adding db_column.'
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A Django team may add `db_column` to an existing model field after deployment so the model definition explicitly documents the column name already in use in the database.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  When `AlterField` adds only a `db_column` attribute and that attribute resolves to the same column name Django was already using, the migration should be treated as a no-op at the schema level. Developers should be able to make that metadata change without triggering an unnecessary column alteration, table rebuild, or backend-specific migration failure.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  The migration state should record the field with its explicit `db_column`, but applying the migration should not emit real schema changes unless some other part of the field definition also changed.
16	
17	  '

title: 'Fixed #21181 -- Added Collate database function.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Django developers often need database-level collation control when filtering or ordering text, for example to do case-insensitive matching or locale-aware sorting without dropping down to raw SQL.


  ## Desired outcome

  Django should provide a first-class `Collate` database function that can be used in ORM expressions for filtering and ordering across supported backends. Developers should be able to request case-insensitive, case-sensitive, or backend-provided locale collations through the ORM and receive backend-appropriate behavior, while invalid collation names still fail clearly.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Queries should support workflows like the case-insensitive filter and ordering scenarios covered by `test_collate_filter_ci`, `test_collate_order_by_cs`, and `test_language_collation_order_by`, and unsupported collations should still raise an error instead of being silently ignored.

  '
title: 'Fixed #32068 -- Added error messages on get() with filters following union(), intersection(), and difference().'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Django developer working with combined querysets expects unsupported operations to fail with a precise explanation. Right now calling `.get()` with filters after `union()`, `intersection()`, or `difference()` does not clearly tell the developer that this pattern is unsupported.


  ## Desired outcome

  If `.get()` is invoked with additional filters on a combined queryset, Django should raise a `NotSupportedError` that explicitly names the combinator involved.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Filtering after `union()`, `intersection()`, or `difference()` triggers `NotSupportedError` with the exact contract message `Calling QuerySet.get(...) with filters after <combinator>() is not supported.` instead of failing ambiguously.

  '

1	title: 'Fixed #6517 -- Made dbshell use charset option on MySQL.'
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Django developers who launch `dbshell` against MySQL expect the CLI session to honor the database charset configured in `OPTIONS`. At the moment that connection detail is ignored, so shell sessions may not match the application’s character encoding.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Have the MySQL `dbshell` command pass the configured charset through to the client process.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  When `OPTIONS[''charset'']` is set, the generated MySQL client command line includes `--default-character-set=<charset>` so interactive shell sessions use the same encoding configuration as the Django connection.
16	
17	  '

You are implementing change requests in a checkout of the Django web framework (version 3.2.0 alpha era). The main checkout is /workspace — NEVER edit files in /workspace or run git commands there. A private git worktree has already been created for you; all your work happens inside it.

Your assigned requirement slugs (comma-separated): greatest-test-cleanup,hidden-m2m-related-name-collisions

Setup:
- The FIRST slug in your list is your worktree name: your worktree is at /tmp/wt/<first-slug> (verify with `ls /tmp/wt`). Start with `cd /tmp/wt/<first-slug> && git checkout -b impl/<first-slug>`.
- Each slug corresponds to /workspace/requirements/<slug>.yaml — read each file fully (it has title, context, desired outcome, acceptance signals). These correspond to real Django bug fixes/features from the 3.1/3.2 era.
- /tmp/leftover.patch (755 lines) contains uncommitted partial work from a previous run. It may already contain an implementation of one of your requirements — check with `grep -n <keyword> /tmp/leftover.patch` before starting from scratch, but verify correctness yourself.

For EACH assigned slug, one at a time, in order:
1. Read the yaml. Explore the relevant code in your worktree (mirror of /workspace at git ref master).
2. Implement the change minimally, following Django's existing code style. If the yaml implies regression tests (most do — "Acceptance signals" often describes a specific test behavior), add/adjust tests in the worktree's tests/ directory too, mirroring where Django keeps tests for that area.
3. Verify by running FOCUSED tests only. Critical: Django is pip-installed from /workspace, so you MUST force the worktree code onto the path. Run from the worktree's tests dir like:
   `cd /tmp/wt/<first-slug>/tests && PYTHONPATH=/tmp/wt/<first-slug> python runtests.py <test.module.path> --parallel 1`
   Confirm the output says "Testing against Django installed in '/tmp/wt/...". Python is `python` (3.9). Only sqlite-backed tests work; do not attempt postgres/mysql/oracle/gis test runs — if a requirement targets another database backend, implement carefully by code inspection and run only database-agnostic checks (e.g. import checks, related unit tests that run on sqlite, or inspection tests that don't need a live DB).
4. Commit ONLY that requirement's changes: `cd /tmp/wt/<first-slug> && git add -A && git commit -m "impl: <slug>"`. Each requirement must be its own separate commit.

Rules:
- Never touch /workspace, other /tmp/wt/* worktrees, or requirement_patches. No git push, no branch switching outside your worktree, no merge/rebase.
- Keep each commit scoped strictly to its requirement; don't fix unrelated things.
- Only commit a requirement when you believe it is correctly and completely implemented (tests passing, or untestable-by-environment with solid code-inspection justification). If genuinely blocked, do NOT commit half-baked work for it — report it as blocked with a precise diagnosis.
- Some requirements depend on others being implemented; your worktree is based on master which has only 3 done (atomic-durable-argument, has-perm-obj-argument, on-commit-callable-typeerror). If your change builds on a pending one, implement your part assuming sane integration and note the dependency in your report.

Final report (concise, per slug): commit hash, files changed, exact test command(s) run and pass/fail result, and any dependency or risk notes.

2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A Django admin user may apply `EmptyFieldListFilter` to reverse relations such as reverse one-to-one or reverse foreign-key links in order to find records that do or do not have related objects.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome

10	  Those filters should work like other empty-value filters instead of crashing when the relation is traversed in reverse. Admin changelists should be able to answer questions like whether an object has an `ImprovedBook` or contributed books without breaking the page.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Using `EmptyFieldListFilter` on reverse relationships should return the expected filtered object sets for both empty and non-empty cases, rather than raising an exception while building the changelist.

1	title: 'Fixed #32116 -- Fixed QuerySet.order_by() crash on EmptyQuerySet with union() on a single non-empty ordered queryset.'
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A Django developer may union an `EmptyQuerySet` with a single ordered queryset and then call `order_by()` on the result, expecting it to behave like the non-empty queryset. Right now Django can crash instead of treating that case as the obvious single-query result.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  When `EmptyQuerySet.union()` is given exactly one non-empty queryset, Django should return that queryset directly so later ordering works normally.
11

14	
15	  `Number.objects.none().union(qs1).order_by(''num'')` yields the same rows as `qs1` when `qs1` is already ordered, rather than crashing because Django tried to preserve a compound-query wrapper unnecessarily.
16	
17	  '

You are implementing change requests in a checkout of the Django web framework (version 3.2.0 alpha era). The main checkout is /workspace — NEVER edit files in /workspace or run git commands there. A private git worktree has already been created for you; all your work happens inside it.

Your assigned requirement slugs (comma-separated): html-count-root-element,httpresponse-docs-grammar

Setup:
- The FIRST slug in your list is your worktree name: your worktree is at /tmp/wt/<first-slug> (verify with `ls /tmp/wt`). Start with `cd /tmp/wt/<first-slug> && git checkout -b impl/<first-slug>`.
- Each slug corresponds to /workspace/requirements/<slug>.yaml — read each file fully (it has title, context, desired outcome, acceptance signals). These correspond to real Django bug fixes/features from the 3.1/3.2 era.
- /tmp/leftover.patch (755 lines) contains uncommitted partial work from a previous run. It may already contain an implementation of one of your requirements — check with `grep -n <keyword> /tmp/leftover.patch` before starting from scratch, but verify correctness yourself.

For EACH assigned slug, one at a time, in order:
1. Read the yaml. Explore the relevant code in your worktree (mirror of /workspace at git ref master).
2. Implement the change minimally, following Django's existing code style. If the yaml implies regression tests (most do — "Acceptance signals" often describes a specific test behavior), add/adjust tests in the worktree's tests/ directory too, mirroring where Django keeps tests for that area.
3. Verify by running FOCUSED tests only. Critical: Django is pip-installed from /workspace, so you MUST force the worktree code onto the path. Run from the worktree's tests dir like:
   `cd /tmp/wt/<first-slug>/tests && PYTHONPATH=/tmp/wt/<first-slug> python runtests.py <test.module.path> --parallel 1`
   Confirm the output says "Testing against Django installed in '/tmp/wt/...". Python is `python` (3.9). Only sqlite-backed tests work; do not attempt postgres/mysql/oracle/gis test runs — if a requirement targets another database backend, implement carefully by code inspection and run only database-agnostic checks (e.g. import checks, related unit tests that run on sqlite, or inspection tests that don't need a live DB).
4. Commit ONLY that requirement's changes: `cd /tmp/wt/<first-slug> && git add -A && git commit -m "impl: <slug>"`. Each requirement must be its own separate commit.

Rules:
- Never touch /workspace, other /tmp/wt/* worktrees, or requirement_patches. No git push, no branch switching outside your worktree, no merge/rebase.
- Keep each commit scoped strictly to its requirement; don't fix unrelated things.
- Only commit a requirement when you believe it is correctly and completely implemented (tests passing, or untestable-by-environment with solid code-inspection justification). If genuinely blocked, do NOT commit half-baked work for it — report it as blocked with a precise diagnosis.
- Some requirements depend on others being implemented; your worktree is based on master which has only 3 done (atomic-durable-argument, has-perm-obj-argument, on-commit-callable-typeerror). If your change builds on a pending one, implement your part assuming sane integration and note the dependency in your report.

Final report (concise, per slug): commit hash, files changed, exact test command(s) run and pass/fail result, and any dependency or risk notes.

title: 'Fixed #26615 -- Made password reset token invalidate when changing email.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users expect a password reset link to stop working after they change the email address associated with the account, because the email identity used for recovery has changed. Django’s current token logic does not consistently invalidate existing reset tokens when only the email changes.


  ## Desired outcome

  Include the user’s current email identity in the password-reset token hash so changing the email address invalidates previously issued tokens, including custom user models that expose their email field through `get_email_field_name()`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A token created by `PasswordResetTokenGenerator` becomes invalid after the user’s email is changed and saved, for both the built-in `User` model and custom users such as `CustomEmailField`, even when the original email was `None`.

  '

title: 'Fixed #32038 -- Fixed EmptyFieldListFilter crash with GenericRelation.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Django admin users often rely on `EmptyFieldListFilter` to find records that do or do not have related content, but applying that filter to a `GenericRelation` currently crashes instead of returning the expected rows. That makes common admin filtering impossible for generic relationships.


  ## Desired outcome

  `EmptyFieldListFilter` should treat `GenericRelation` as a nullable reverse relation so admins can filter for items with or without related objects.


  ## Acceptance signals

title: 'Fixed #32120 -- Added DatabaseFeatures.indexes_foreign_keys.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Database backends differ on whether foreign-key columns can be indexed and introspected in a way Django should treat as ordinary indexes. Backend authors need a first-class feature flag instead of scattered backend-specific assumptions.


  ## Desired outcome

  Add `DatabaseFeatures.indexes_foreign_keys` so Django can ask each backend explicitly whether foreign keys are indexed in the normal backend-specific way.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Backends expose `indexes_foreign_keys` as part of their feature contract, and code that reasons about index presence can rely on that flag instead of hard-coded vendor checks.

  '
title: 'Fixed #32042 -- Improved error messages for the number of submitted forms in formsets.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When a formset submission violates minimum or maximum form counts, Django shows a generic message that reads awkwardly and does not distinguish singular from plural cases. Developers surface these errors directly to users, so the phrasing needs to be clearer and grammatically correct.


  ## Desired outcome

  Formsets should report these validation failures using explicit “at most” and “at least” wording, with correct singular and plural forms.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Exceeding the maximum raises the non-form errors `Please submit at most 1 form.` or `Please submit at most N forms.` as appropriate, and falling below the minimum raises `Please submit at least 1 form.` or `Please submit at least N forms.` instead of the older “or fewer/or more” phrasing.

  '

1	title: 'Fixed #32105 -- Added template paths as ExceptionReporter class attributes.'
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Teams that customize Django’s debug reporting sometimes want to swap only the technical 500 templates while keeping the rest of `ExceptionReporter` intact. Today that requires copying the rendering methods instead of overriding a simple attribute.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Make the template locations on `ExceptionReporter` overridable through class attributes so custom reporters can replace either the HTML or text technical 500 template without reimplementing rendering logic.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  `ExceptionReporter` exposes `html_template_path` and `text_template_path`, and a subclass can point those attributes at custom templates so the debug page renders alternate text such as `Oh no, an error occurred!` and `Oh dear, an error occurred!` without overriding `get_traceback_html()` or `get_traceback_text()`.
16	
17	  '

1	title: 'Fixed #31902 -- Fixed crash of ExclusionConstraint on expressions with params.'
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A Django developer using PostgreSQL exclusion constraints may build them from expressions that include parameters, such as function calls or transformed values.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  `ExclusionConstraint` should support those parameterized expressions when generating schema SQL instead of crashing while assembling the constraint definition. Expression parameters need to be quoted into the emitted SQL so the final constraint can be created normally.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Applying a migration with an exclusion constraint built from parameterized expressions should succeed, and the named constraint should appear in database introspection results rather than failing during SQL generation.
16	
17	  '

title: 'Fixed #32098 -- Made FieldFile use FileField.attname.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Developers sometimes customize file fields so the storage descriptor is attached differently from the field’s attribute name, and `FieldFile` should honor that lower-level storage contract. Right now save and delete flows can write back through `FileField.name` instead of `FileField.attname`, which breaks those customizations.


  ## Desired outcome

  `FieldFile` should update model instances through `FileField.attname` whenever it stores or clears the file value.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After `FieldFile.save()` or `FieldFile.delete()`, the instance attribute tracked by `self.field.attname` reflects the new value or `None`, allowing custom file-field descriptors to work correctly.

  '
title: 'Fixed #31941 -- Corrected FileField.deconstruct() with a callable storage.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Django models can be configured with a callable storage factory so file handling is created lazily, which is important for settings-dependent storage configuration and migrations.


  ## Desired outcome

  When a `FileField` is deconstructed for migrations, Django should preserve the original callable in the field definition instead of serializing the already evaluated storage instance. This keeps migration state faithful to the model declaration and prevents spurious migration churn.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Deconstructing a field configured with a callable storage should return that callable under the `storage` keyword argument, not the instantiated storage object produced at runtime.

  '

title: 'Fixed #27906 -- Fixed count of RootElement in test.html.count().'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Django’s HTML test helpers are supposed to let developers assert that one fragment appears inside a larger HTML structure, but `html.count()` currently misses valid matches when the searched fragment is a sequence of sibling elements inside a larger root element. That makes assertions undercount patterns like `''<a/><b/>''` within `''<a/><b/><c/>''`.


  ## Desired outcome

  Element sequences wrapped as a root fragment should be counted wherever that ordered sequence appears among a larger element’s children, including repeated matches and matches nested under different parents.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `parse_html(...).count(...)` correctly finds sibling sequences such as `''<a/><b/>''` inside `''<a/><b/><c/>''`, counts repeated occurrences, still returns zero for non-matching orderings, and preserves existing behavior for exact subtree matches.

  '

title: 'Refs #32074 -- Fixed handling memoryview content by HttpResponse on Python 3.10+.'
category: bugfix
requirement: 'Django applications should be able to assign a `memoryview` directly to `HttpResponse.content` and get the original binary payload back unchanged, including on Python versions where `memoryview` has become iterable. A `memoryview` must be treated like a bytes-like value rather than being consumed chunk-by-chunk as though it were a stream of separate response parts, because that changes the payload unexpectedly. The result should be that `HttpResponse` preserves `memoryview` content correctly across supported Python versions.

title: 'Fixed #31918 -- Allowed QuerySet.in_bulk() to fetch on a single distinct field.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Django developer may use `distinct(''headline'')` and then want `in_bulk(field_name=''headline'')` to map results by that same distinct field.


  ## Desired outcome

  `QuerySet.in_bulk()` should allow this when the queryset is distinct on exactly one field and that field matches `field_name`, because the result set is effectively unique for that key. It should still reject cases where uniqueness is not guaranteed, such as a distinct clause covering multiple fields while requesting a different key.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A queryset distinct on a single field should be convertible into a bulk mapping keyed by that field, while unsupported cases continue to raise `ValueError` with the existing message that the requested `field_name` is not unique.

  '

title: 'Fixed #31919 -- Resolved output_field of IntegerField subclasses combinations.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Django expression users often combine integer-like fields such as `IntegerField` and `AutoField` and expect Django to infer a sensible numeric result type automatically.


  ## Desired outcome

  When integer subclasses are combined in expressions, Django should resolve `output_field` consistently instead of producing the wrong type or leaving the result ambiguous. Integer-family combinations like `IntegerField` with `AutoField` should still be treated as integer results.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Mixed integer-subclass expressions should infer an integer output field in both directions, including the combinations covered by `IntegerField` plus `AutoField` and `AutoField` plus `IntegerField`.

  '
title: 'Fixed #22276 -- Fixed crash when formset  management form is invalid.'
category: bugfix
requirement: 'A broken or tampered formset management form should not crash a page while Django is validating submitted data. When the management data is missing or invalid, `formset.is_valid()` should return `False` and expose the problem through `non_form_errors()` using the `missing_management_form` error key, rather than raising an exception before the view can handle the submission. Developers also need to be able to override that message through the formset `error_messages` argument, while Django’s default text remains `ManagementForm data is missing or has been tampered with. Missing fields: %(field_names)s. You may need to file a bug report if the issue persists.` so the missing hidden fields are still spelled out.

  '

  Django developers using `JSONField` key transforms often expect `__in` filters to behave consistently across PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, and Oracle.


  ## Desired outcome

  Applying `__in` to a key transform should work on backends without a native JSON type as well, including values that need backend-specific extraction or quoting. The ORM should generate the proper JSON wrapper expressions automatically instead of crashing or miscompiling the lookup.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Queries using key-transform `__in` should work across the supported non-native JSON backends, with Django choosing the correct SQL form such as JSON extraction or query/value wrappers for each database.

2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A Django developer composing compound querysets expects unsupported ordering in nested set operations to fail cleanly with the usual database error, not crash Django itself. Right now chaining another `union()` onto an already ordered combined queryset can blow up before the database gets a chance to report the unsupported SQL pattern.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Combining querysets should remain stable even when the final SQL is invalid for the backend, and developers should get the normal database error for unsupported ordering inside compound statements.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Calling `union()` on a queryset that already came from `union(...).order_by(...)` no longer crashes Django internals; instead the operation reaches the database layer and raises the expected ordering-related `DatabaseError`.
16	
17	  '

category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Django project on PostgreSQL may attach a custom decoder to `JSONField` and still expect to sort query results by that field.


  ## Desired outcome

  Ordering by a `JSONField` should continue to work even when the connection has a custom JSON decoder, instead of crashing because PostgreSQL values are decoded too early for the ordering SQL Django needs. Django should preserve raw ordering behavior while still supporting decoded reads where appropriate.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A queryset ordered by a `JSONField` with a custom decoder configured should execute successfully rather than failing during result handling or SQL generation.

  '

title: 'Refs #9061, Refs #20347 -- Added absolute_max and can_delete_extra arguments to generic_inlineformset_factory().'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Developers using generic inline formsets need the same control over form-count limits and deletion behavior that standard inline formsets already provide, especially in admin-like editing interfaces.


  ## Desired outcome

  `generic_inlineformset_factory()` should accept both `absolute_max` and `can_delete_extra` so callers can cap how many submitted forms are ever processed and decide whether extra forms may expose a `DELETE` control. This should behave like the rest of Django''s inline formset APIs rather than forcing generic relations into a less capable variant.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A formset created through `generic_inlineformset_factory()` should honor `can_delete_extra=False` by omitting `DELETE` from extra forms, and should honor `absolute_max` the same way non-generic inline formsets do.

  '
title: Added DatabaseFeatures.can_alter_geometry_field.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  GIS backends do not all support altering geometry columns in-place, but migration and test code currently has to infer that capability indirectly. Backend authors need an explicit feature flag for whether geometry field alteration is supported.


  ## Desired outcome

  Expose a `DatabaseFeatures.can_alter_geometry_field` capability on GIS backends so schema operations and tests can branch on that support directly.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Spatial backends advertise `can_alter_geometry_field` through their features class, allowing code that performs geometry-field schema changes to distinguish supported backends from ones that require a different path.

  '

1	title: 'Fixed #32073 -- Skipped collation tests on PostgreSQL < 10.'
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Older PostgreSQL servers do not support ICU collations, but Django’s backend feature flags can still advertise language-collation test data as though they do. That makes backend-specific tests fail for capability reasons rather than real regressions.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Expose language-collation test fixtures only on PostgreSQL versions that actually support them, so inspection and schema tests skip cleanly on older servers.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  On PostgreSQL 10+ the backend still exposes the `non_default` and `swedish_ci` test collations, while older PostgreSQL versions return no language-collation entries and the dependent tests are skipped rather than failing.
16	
17	  '

1	title: 'Fixed #32130 -- Fixed pre-Django 3.1 password reset tokens validation.'
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: 'Sites that upgraded to Django 3.1 should not strand users who are still following password-reset links generated by an earlier Django release. A password reset token created before Django 3.1 must continue to validate for the remainder of its configured timeout instead of being rejected immediately after the upgrade, as long as the token is otherwise genuine and unexpired. The desired outcome is that `PasswordResetTokenGenerator` accepts both current tokens and legacy pre-3.1 tokens during the compatibility window so password reset emails already in users’ inboxes keep working.
4	
5	  '

3	requirement: 'Developers running `makemessages` need a clear signal when they pass an invalid locale code with `--locale`, because a hyphenated value such as `pl-PL` is not a valid Django locale identifier and should not silently produce confusing results. Instead of trying to process that locale, the command should skip it and print an actionable warning in the form `invalid locale %s, did you mean %s?`, pointing the user to the underscore-based locale name. Valid locales should continue to be processed normally, while invalid hyphenated ones are ignored before any extraction work starts.

1	title: 'Fixed #13060 -- Improved error message when ManagementForm data is missing.'
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: 'When a developer submits a formset with the management data missing or under the wrong prefix, Django currently raises an error that tells them something is wrong but not which hidden fields are actually absent, which makes bad prefixes and broken JavaScript formset handling unnecessarily hard to diagnose. The formset should still fail with the existing `missing_management_form` validation code, but the message needs to spell out the missing field names directly in the text so the developer can immediately see entries such as `form-TOTAL_FORMS` and `form-INITIAL_FORMS` instead of reverse-engineering the problem. The expected result is a clearer, user-facing `ManagementForm data is missing or has been tampered with. Missing fields: %(field_names)s` error that points straight at the missing management inputs.
4	
5	  '

title: 'Fixed #32179 -- Added JSONObject database function.'
category: bugfix
requirement: 'Django developers need a database function for constructing JSON objects directly in queryset annotations and aggregates without falling back to handwritten backend-specific SQL. Add a public `JSONObject` function that can build empty objects, simple key/value objects, nested objects, and objects whose values come from expressions such as `F()`, `Value()`, or other database functions, while respecting backend support through the `has_json_object_function` feature flag. On databases that do not support it, Django should raise `NotSupportedError` with the exact message `JSONObject() is not supported on this database backend.` so callers get a clear, consistent failure mode.

  '

class RedirectCycleError(Exception):
    """The test client has been asked to follow a redirect loop."""
    def __init__(self, message, last_response):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.last_response = last_response
        self.redirect_chain = last_response.redirect_chain


class FakePayload:
    """
    A wrapper around BytesIO that restricts what can be read since data from
    the network can't be sought and cannot be read outside of its content
    length. This makes sure that views can't do anything under the test client
    that wouldn't work in real life.
    """
    def __init__(self, content=None):
        self.__content = BytesIO()
        self.__len = 0
        self.read_started = False
        if content is not None:
            self.write(content)

    def __len__(self):
        return self.__len

    def read(self, num_bytes=None):
        if not self.read_started:
            self.__content.seek(0)
            self.read_started = True
        if num_bytes is None:
            num_bytes = self.__len or 0
        assert self.__len >= num_bytes, "Cannot read more than the available bytes from the HTTP incoming data."
        content = self.__content.read(num_bytes)
        self.__len -= num_bytes
        return content

    def write(self, content):
        if self.read_started:
            raise ValueError("Unable to write a payload after it's been read")
        content = force_bytes(content)
        self.__content.write(content)
        self.__len += len(content)


def closing_iterator_wrapper(iterable, close):
    try:
        yield from iterable
    finally:
        request_finished.disconnect(close_old_connections)
        close()                                 # will fire request_finished
        request_finished.connect(close_old_connections)


def conditional_content_removal(request, response):
    """
    Simulate the behavior of most Web servers by removing the content of
    responses for HEAD requests, 1xx, 204, and 304 responses. Ensure
    compliance with RFC 7230, section 3.3.3.
    """
    if 100 <= response.status_code < 200 or response.status_code in (204, 304):
        if response.streaming:
            response.streaming_content = []
        else:
            response.content = b''
    if request.method == 'HEAD':
        if response.streaming:
            response.streaming_content = []
        else:
            response.content = b''
    return response


class ClientHandler(BaseHandler):

    interface to compose requests, but return the raw HttpResponse object with
    the originating WSGIRequest attached to its ``wsgi_request`` attribute.
    """

title: 'Fixed #32007 -- Fixed queryset crash with Q() annotation and aggregation.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Django developer can annotate a queryset with boolean logic and aggregate over the same queryset, but a regression now makes that pattern crash when the annotation is built from a `Q()` expression. This breaks otherwise legitimate reporting queries that mix condition flags with aggregate counts.


  ## Desired outcome

  Querysets that combine an aggregation with a `Q()`-based annotation should execute normally instead of failing during query construction.


  ## Acceptance signals

  An annotation created with `ExpressionWrapper(Q(...), output_field=BooleanField())` can live alongside `Count(...)` on the same queryset, and the resulting row returns both the boolean annotation and aggregate value without crashing.

  '
title: 'Fixed #31990 -- Fixed QuerySet.ordered for GROUP BY queries on models with Meta.ordering.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Django developer using aggregation expects to be able to tell whether a queryset is genuinely ordered before relying on that ordering for pagination, slicing, or downstream query composition. Right now `QuerySet.ordered` incorrectly reports `True` for `GROUP BY` style queries such as annotated querysets and `.values().annotate()` on models that define `Meta.ordering`, even though that default ordering does not actually apply.


  ## Desired outcome

  When a queryset’s only apparent ordering comes from `Meta.ordering`, `QuerySet.ordered` should stay `False` for grouped queries and only become `True` once the developer explicitly orders the queryset.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Both a plain annotated queryset and a `.values(...).annotate(...)` queryset report `QuerySet.ordered` as `False`, and adding an explicit `.order_by(''name'')` flips the same queries to `True`.

  '

This gives operators a reliable breadcrumb when robust signal handlers misbehave.

title: 'Fixed #32046 -- Added CreateCollation/RemoveCollation operations for PostgreSQL.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  PostgreSQL users sometimes need a migration-managed way to add or remove database collations so locale-sensitive ordering and comparisons can be deployed alongside schema changes. Until now Django has not exposed first-class migration operations for that workflow.


  ## Desired outcome

  Provide dedicated PostgreSQL migration operations named `CreateCollation` and `RemoveCollation` so projects can manage collations in migrations, including provider and determinism options where the server supports them.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `CreateCollation` and `RemoveCollation` are importable from `django.contrib.postgres.operations`, they serialize cleanly in migrations, and unsupported combinations fail with the documented messages `Non-deterministic collations require PostgreSQL 12+.` and `Non-libc providers require PostgreSQL 10+.` rather than silently generating invalid SQL.

  '
title: Added DatabaseIntrospection.index_default_access_method on the PostgreSQL backend.
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Teams building PostgreSQL-derived backends need Django’s introspection layer to understand what index access method counts as the backend’s default so schema inspection doesn’t misclassify ordinary indexes as custom ones. Today that assumption is hard-coded to `btree`, which blocks compatible backends that use a different default access method.


  ## Desired outcome

  Expose a backend hook named `DatabaseIntrospection.index_default_access_method` so PostgreSQL-family backends can declare their own default index method and have constraint introspection treat it as the ordinary case.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The PostgreSQL backend continues to use `btree` by default, but a subclass can override `DatabaseIntrospection.index_default_access_method` and have introspected index ordering and basic-index detection follow that declared default instead of a hard-coded name.

  '

title: 'Fixed #32012 -- Made test database creation sync apps models when migrations are disabled.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Teams that speed up their test suite by setting `TEST[''MIGRATE''] = False` still expect Django to create tables for installed apps in the temporary test database. Right now apps without migrations can be left unsynchronized in that mode, so tests start against an incomplete schema.


  ## Desired outcome

  When test database creation runs with migrations disabled, Django should still sync application models into the test database as if all apps had migrations temporarily disabled through `MIGRATION_MODULES`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  With `TEST[''MIGRATE'']` set to `False`, installed app models are present in the created test database, and Django restores the previous `MIGRATION_MODULES` configuration after setup instead of leaking the temporary override.

  '

title: 'Refs #31672 -- Made technical 500 debug page include exceptions without tracebacks.'
category: bugfix
requirement: 'When Django renders the technical 500 debug page for an exception that has no traceback attached, developers should still see a complete report instead of a broken or misleading traceback section. The debug page and plain-text report need to include those exceptions explicitly, using `None` for the first missing traceback marker and `Traceback: None` for later chained exceptions, so the exception itself and any cause chain remain visible even without frame data. The desired outcome is a stable technical 500 view that can display traceback-less exceptions clearly rather than failing to render useful diagnostic output.

  '
title: 'Fixed #31674 -- Fixed displaying traceback in technical 500 debug page.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When Django shows the technical 500 page in debug mode, developers depend on the traceback being present even if the exception chain includes another exception object that has no traceback of its own. Right now that situation can hide the main traceback and make debugging much harder.


  ## Desired outcome

  The debug error page should still render the real traceback and chained-exception explanation even when part of the exception chain lacks traceback data.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `ExceptionReporter.get_traceback_frames()` still returns the available frames for the real exception, and the HTML debug page includes the traceback section plus the chained-message text `During handling of the above exception (My context), another exception occurred` instead of dropping the traceback entirely.

  '

title: 'Fixed #31947 -- Made QuerySet.update_or_create() reuse get_or_create().'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Django developers use `update_or_create()` for atomic upsert-like behavior and expect it to share the same correctness guarantees as `get_or_create()` around races and object creation.


  ## Desired outcome

  `update_or_create()` should reuse `get_or_create()` internally rather than duplicating a slightly different creation path. That keeps locking, callable default resolution, and integrity-error recovery aligned between the two APIs while preserving the usual update behavior when the object already exists.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Creating a missing object through `update_or_create()` should follow the same transaction and conflict-handling semantics as `get_or_create()`, while existing rows should still be updated and returned with the expected `(object, created)` contract.

  '

title: 'Fixed #31382 -- Made Model.save(update_fields=...) raise ValueError on non-concrete fields.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Django developer may call `Model.save(update_fields=[...])` to limit an update to concrete database columns, but mistakes in that list can currently be hard to diagnose.


  ## Desired outcome

  If `update_fields` contains a many-to-many field, a nonexistent name, or a non-concrete field that has no database column, `Model.save()` should fail immediately with a `ValueError` instead of proceeding as though the request were valid. The error message should make clear that these names are not acceptable update targets.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Passing a non-concrete field such as `non_concrete` should raise `ValueError` with the message beginning `The following fields do not exist in this model, are m2m fields, or are non-concrete fields:` so developers can correct the field list before data is written.

  '
title: 'Fixed #32304 -- Fixed prefixing STATIC_URL and MEDIA_URL by SCRIPT_NAME for absolute URLs with no domain.'
category: bugfix
requirement: 'Deployments mounted under a `SCRIPT_NAME` prefix should not have that prefix incorrectly prepended to absolute `STATIC_URL` or `MEDIA_URL` values that already start with `http://`, `https://`, or `/`. Django should continue prefixing only relative asset URLs, while absolute paths and fully qualified URLs remain exactly as configured. This prevents broken asset links in setups that serve static or media files from a fixed absolute location.

  '

title: 'Fixed #31640 -- Made Trunc() truncate datetimes to Date/TimeField in a specific timezone.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Django developer truncating datetimes in a specific timezone expects to be able to target `DateField` or `TimeField` output directly, not just `DateTimeField`. Right now `Trunc()` can ignore that expectation or fail when timezone-aware truncation is requested for date-only or time-only results.


  ## Desired outcome

  Allow `Trunc()` to truncate a `DateTimeField` into `DateField` or `TimeField` output in a specific timezone, across supported database backends, while keeping timezone validation strict for non-datetime inputs.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Queries such as `Trunc(''start_datetime'', kind, output_field=DateField(), tzinfo=...)` and the corresponding `TimeField()` form return correctly truncated values in the requested timezone, instead of behaving only like datetime truncation or refusing the conversion.

  '

title: 'Fixed #32182 -- Fixed crash of JSONField nested key transforms with subquery annotations on PostgreSQL.'
category: bugfix
requirement: 'Django developers using PostgreSQL `JSONField` annotations should be able to drill into nested keys even when the JSON value comes from a `Subquery()` annotation, instead of hitting a query-construction crash. A queryset that annotates a JSON value from a subquery and then applies chained transforms such as `KeyTransform(''d'', ''subquery_value'')` followed by another nested key lookup should execute normally and return the expected rows. The goal is for nested JSON key access on subquery-produced values to behave the same way it already does for direct fields and other JSON expressions.

  '

title: 'Fixed #32080 -- Fixed displaying Unicode chars in forms.JSONField and read-only JSONField values in admin.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Django developers and admin users expect JSON values containing real Unicode characters or emoji to be shown as readable text, not escaped ASCII sequences. Right now `forms.JSONField` and read-only admin displays can turn those values into harder-to-read escaped output.


  ## Desired outcome

  Preserve Unicode characters when JSON is prepared for form display or rendered read-only in the admin, while still using the field’s configured JSON encoder.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `JSONField.prepare_value()` returns strings like `"你好，世界"`, `{"a": "😀🐱"}`, and `["你好，世界", "jaźń"]` without ASCII-escaping them, and read-only admin rendering for `models.JSONField` uses the same readable `ensure_ascii=False` behavior.

  '

title: 'Refs #31358 -- Added constant for get_random_string()''s default alphabet.'
category: feature
requirement: 'Code that needs Django''s default random-string alphabet should be able to reference a named constant instead of depending on a duplicated literal. Expose a constant for `get_random_string()`''s default alphabet so callers and internal code can share the same contract while leaving the actual default-character behavior unchanged. This is a small developer-facing API cleanup aimed at consistency, not a behavior change.

  '
title: 'Fixed #32134 -- Fixed crash of __range lookup with namedtuple.'
category: bugfix
requirement: 'Django developers sometimes pass structured tuples into queryset filters, and a `__range` lookup should treat a `namedtuple` the same way it treats any other two-value range. Right now that lookup can crash while resolving the values instead of building the query, even though the caller supplied a valid lower and upper bound. The ORM should preserve `namedtuple` inputs and resolve their contents correctly so range filters execute normally rather than failing during query construction.

  '

title: 'Refs #32178 -- Changed BaseDatabaseFeatures.django_test_expected_failures to set().'
category: feature
requirement: 'Backends and test infrastructure code should be able to treat `BaseDatabaseFeatures.django_test_expected_failures` as a set-based collection instead of a list-like container. This is a small developer-facing API cleanup: the default value should be `set()` so membership checks and extensions behave consistently, without changing which tests are actually expected to fail on any backend. Existing semantics should stay the same apart from the container type.

  '

title: 'Fixed #31825 -- Made RenameField operation a noop for fields with db_column.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Django developer renaming model fields in migrations may keep a stable database column name by setting `db_column`, especially when preserving compatibility with existing tables or hand-managed SQL.


  ## Desired outcome

  If a migration uses `RenameField` only to change the Python attribute name while the underlying column name stays the same because `db_column` is fixed, Django should treat that as a metadata-only change instead of issuing unnecessary schema edits. The rename should still update migration state correctly, including renamed related fields such as `renamed_field` and `renamed_fk_field`, but the database layer should not try to rebuild or rename a column that has not actually changed.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Running the migration should complete without redundant ALTER TABLE work on backends that special-case field renames, and projects that rely on a stable `db_column` should see the model state reflect the new field names while the physical column remains untouched.

  '

title: 'Fixed #31831 -- Fixed migration operations ordering when adding order_with_respect_to and constraints/indexes.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Django developer relying on autogenerated migrations may add `order_with_respect_to` at the same time as new indexes or constraints on the same model.


  ## Desired outcome

  The migration autodetector should generate operations in a dependency-safe order so that `AlterOrderWithRespectTo` is applied before any indexes or constraints that depend on the `_order` column it introduces. Projects should be able to add ordering plus related constraints in one model change without hand-editing the migration plan or getting operations sequenced incorrectly.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Autogenerated migrations for these combinations should place `AlterOrderWithRespectTo` early enough for follow-on index and constraint operations to succeed, including cases reflected by scenarios like `test_add_model_order_with_respect_to_index_constraint` and `test_set_alter_order_with_respect_to_index_constraint_foo_together`.

  '

class RequestFactory:
    """
    Class that lets you create mock Request objects for use in testing.

    Usage:

    rf = RequestFactory()
    get_request = rf.get('/hello/')
    post_request = rf.post('/submit/', {'foo': 'bar'})

    Once you have a request object you can pass it to any view function,
    just as if that view had been hooked up using a URLconf.
    """
    def __init__(self, *, json_encoder=DjangoJSONEncoder, **defaults):
        self.json_encoder = json_encoder
        self.defaults = defaults
        self.cookies = SimpleCookie()
        self.errors = BytesIO()

    def _base_environ(self, **request):
        """
        The base environment for a request.
        """
        # This is a minimal valid WSGI environ dictionary, plus:
        # - HTTP_COOKIE: for cookie support,
        # - REMOTE_ADDR: often useful, see #8551.
        # See https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-3333/#environ-variables
        return {
            'HTTP_COOKIE': '; '.join(sorted(
                '%s=%s' % (morsel.key, morsel.coded_value)
                for morsel in self.cookies.values()
            )),
            'PATH_INFO': '/',
            'REMOTE_ADDR': '127.0.0.1',
            'REQUEST_METHOD': 'GET',
            'SCRIPT_NAME': '',
            'SERVER_NAME': 'testserver',
            'SERVER_PORT': '80',
            'SERVER_PROTOCOL': 'HTTP/1.1',
            'wsgi.version': (1, 0),
            'wsgi.url_scheme': 'http',
            'wsgi.input': FakePayload(b''),
            'wsgi.errors': self.errors,
            'wsgi.multiprocess': True,
            'wsgi.multithread': False,
            'wsgi.run_once': False,
            **self.defaults,
            **request,
        }

    def request(self, **request):
        "Construct a generic request object."
        return WSGIRequest(self._base_environ(**request))

    def _encode_data(self, data, content_type):
        if content_type is MULTIPART_CONTENT:
            return encode_multipart(BOUNDARY, data)
        else:
            # Encode the content so that the byte representation is correct.
            match = CONTENT_TYPE_RE.match(content_type)
            if match:
                charset = match[1]
            else:
                charset = settings.DEFAULT_CHARSET
            return force_bytes(data, encoding=charset)

    def _encode_json(self, data, content_type):
        """
        Return encoded JSON if data is a dict, list, or tuple and content_type
        is application/json.
        """
        should_encode = JSON_CONTENT_TYPE_RE.match(content_type) and isinstance(data, (dict, list, tuple))
        return json.dumps(data, cls=self.json_encoder) if should_encode else data

    def _get_path(self, parsed):
        path = parsed.path
        # If there are parameters, add them
        if parsed.params:
            path += ";" + parsed.params
        path = unquote_to_bytes(path)
        # Replace the behavior where non-ASCII values in the WSGI environ are
        # arbitrarily decoded with ISO-8859-1.
        # Refs comment in `get_bytes_from_wsgi()`.
        return path.decode('iso-8859-1')

    def get(self, path, data=None, secure=False, **extra):
        """Construct a GET request."""
        data = {} if data is None else data
        return self.generic('GET', path, secure=secure, **{
            'QUERY_STRING': urlencode(data, doseq=True),
            **extra,
        })

    def post(self, path, data=None, content_type=MULTIPART_CONTENT,
             secure=False, **extra):
        """Construct a POST request."""
        data = self._encode_json({} if data is None else data, content_type)
        post_data = self._encode_data(data, content_type)

        return self.generic('POST', path, post_data, content_type,
                            secure=secure, **extra)

    def head(self, path, data=None, secure=False, **extra):
        """Construct a HEAD request."""
        data = {} if data is None else data
        return self.generic('HEAD', path, secure=secure, **{
            'QUERY_STRING': urlencode(data, doseq=True),
            **extra,
        })

    def trace(self, path, secure=False, **extra):
        """Construct a TRACE request."""
        return self.generic('TRACE', path, secure=secure, **extra)

    def options(self, path, data='', content_type='application/octet-stream',
                secure=False, **extra):
        "Construct an OPTIONS request."
        return self.generic('OPTIONS', path, data, content_type,
                            secure=secure, **extra)

    def put(self, path, data='', content_type='application/octet-stream',
            secure=False, **extra):
        """Construct a PUT request."""
        data = self._encode_json(data, content_type)
        return self.generic('PUT', path, data, content_type,
                            secure=secure, **extra)

    def patch(self, path, data='', content_type='application/octet-stream',
              secure=False, **extra):

2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Different Python memcached clients expect server locations in slightly different formats, which makes it awkward for Django developers to share cache settings across backends.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Django''s memcached backends should expose a `client_servers` hook so each backend can normalize the configured server list before instantiating its underlying client. 11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Backends should be able to override `client_servers`, and a pylibmc-backed cache should report normalized server values such as `/run/memcached/socket` when given either `unix:/run/memcached/socket` or the plain socket path.

17	  '

title: 'Fixed #31926 -- Fixed recreating queryset with FilteredRelation when using a pickled Query.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Django developer may pickle a queryset’s underlying `Query` object and later reattach it to a fresh queryset, expecting filtered joins to survive that round trip. Right now query reconstruction can break when `FilteredRelation` is involved, so the recreated queryset loses the correct join identity and returns the wrong result or crashes.


  ## Desired outcome

  Filtered relations should remain stable when a query is pickled and restored, including both reverse foreign-key and many-to-many cases.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A queryset that annotates through `models.FilteredRelation(...)`, then round-trips through `pickle.dumps(...query)` and `pickle.loads(...)`, still executes correctly and preserves the filtered aggregate result after the query is attached back to a new queryset.

  '

title: 'Fixed #31928 -- Fixed detecting an async get_response in various middlewares.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Django projects running under ASGI rely on middleware classes to correctly recognize when `get_response` is asynchronous so the request chain is adapted in the right mode.


  ## Desired outcome

  Built-in middlewares should consistently detect coroutine `get_response` callables the same way `MiddlewareMixin` expects, rather than behaving like synchronous middleware just because their initialization path skipped the right setup. This should hold across the cache, security, session, locale, common, gzip, and conditional request middlewares that wrap the standard request path.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When a middleware is constructed around an async `get_response`, it should present itself as coroutine-aware instead of confusing the middleware chain, and the shared middleware tests should be able to run that check across the full built-in middleware set.

  '

title: 'Fixed #31905 -- Made MiddlewareMixin call process_request()/process_response() with thread sensitive.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Django''s async request path can run legacy middleware through `MiddlewareMixin`, and database-connected code in `process_request()` or `process_response()` must stay on the correct thread.


  ## Desired outcome

  When these hooks are adapted for async execution, Django should call them with `thread_sensitive=True` so thread-local resources such as database connections stay consistent. Projects that still depend on synchronous middleware hooks should be able to use them under ASGI without surprising thread hops.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A middleware adapted through `MiddlewareMixin` should execute its request and response hooks on the same thread and connection context throughout the async call chain, matching the guarantee exercised by `test_sync_to_async_uses_base_thread_and_connection`.

  '

184	    kind = None

192	    def as_sql(self, compiler, connection):
193	        inner_sql, inner_params = compiler.compile(self.lhs)
194	        if isinstance(self.output_field, DateTimeField):
195	            tzname = self.get_tzname()
196	            sql = connection.ops.datetime_trunc_sql(self.kind, inner_sql, tzname)
197	        elif isinstance(self.output_field, DateField):
198	            sql = connection.ops.date_trunc_sql(self.kind, inner_sql)
199	        elif isinstance(self.output_field, TimeField):
200	            sql = connection.ops.time_trunc_sql(self.kind, inner_sql)
201	        else:
202	            raise ValueError('Trunc only valid on DateField, TimeField, or DateTimeField.')
203	        return sql, inner_params
204	
205	    def resolve_expression(self, query=None, allow_joins=True, reuse=None, summarize=False, for_save=False):
206	        copy = super().resolve_expression(query, allow_joins, reuse, summarize, for_save)
207	        field = copy.lhs.output_field
208	        # DateTimeField is a subclass of DateField so this works for both.
209	        assert isinstance(field, (DateField, TimeField)), (
210	            "%r isn't a DateField, TimeField, or DateTimeField." % field.name
211	        )
212	        # If self.output_field was None, then accessing the field will trigger
213	        # the resolver to assign it to self.lhs.output_field.
214	        if not isinstance(copy.output_field, (DateField, DateTimeField, TimeField)):
215	            raise ValueError('output_field must be either DateField, TimeField, or DateTimeField')
216	        # Passing dates or times to functions expecting datetimes is most
217	        # likely a mistake.
218	        class_output_field = self.__class__.output_field if isinstance(self.__class__.output_field, Field) else None
219	        output_field = class_output_field or copy.output_field
220	        has_explicit_output_field = class_output_field or field.__class__ is not copy.output_field.__class__
221	        if type(field) == DateField and (
222	                isinstance(output_field, DateTimeField) or copy.kind in ('hour', 'minute', 'second', 'time')):
223	            raise ValueError("Cannot truncate DateField '%s' to %s. " % (
224	                field.name, output_field.__class__.__name__ if has_explicit_output_field else 'DateTimeField'
225	            ))
226	        elif isinstance(field, TimeField) and (
227	                isinstance(output_field, DateTimeField) or
228	                copy.kind in ('year', 'quarter', 'month', 'week', 'day', 'date')):
229	            raise ValueError("Cannot truncate TimeField '%s' to %s. " % (

231	            ))

title: 'Fixed #32094 -- Fixed flush() calls on management command self.stdout/err proxies.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Long-running management commands often flush progress output so operators can see work advancing in real time. Django’s `self.stdout` and `self.stderr` wrappers currently swallow that expectation because calling `flush()` on the proxy does not reliably forward to the underlying stream.


  ## Desired outcome

  Management command output wrappers should expose a working `flush()` method so progress text becomes visible immediately on wrapped output streams.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A command can call `self.stdout.flush()` after `self.stdout.write(''Working...'')`, and the proxy forwards the flush to the wrapped stream before later output such as `OK` is written.

  '

title: 'Fixed #32152 -- Fixed grouping by subquery aliases.'
category: bugfix
requirement: 'Django developers using annotated `Subquery()` expressions in aggregate queries should be able to group on those selected aliases without the ORM falling back to the wrong expression in the generated `GROUP BY` clause. A queryset that selects subquery-based annotations and then groups by them must keep using the chosen subquery aliases consistently, so the SQL stays valid and the results are grouped on the values the developer explicitly selected. The expected outcome is that `Subquery()` aliases participate in `GROUP BY` the same way other selected annotations do, instead of breaking grouped queries after annotation masking or selection changes.

  '
